x: T. Hampson won the 1930 A.A.A. half mile in 1m. 53.1s. but was first claim for Achilles (perhaps we should make a special case of Achilles members?).
Great Britain had two winners only, our Tommy Green, and Tom Hampson (800 metres) who was a second-chain Belgrave man, and scored in some of our Surrey County Relay wins.

Tommy Scrimshaw for his outstanding athletic career and tussles with the great Tommy Hampson at Stamford Bridge. To each and everyone, Alf's memories would be of the great times we had and the pleasure from each others company, the arguments we had and above all the enormous team spirit for the Club to succeed.

Aged 62, ex-international who ran so many times for Great Britain with the great Tommy Hampson, gold medallist at the 1932 Olympic Games. Jack last saw Dickie a few days after he had joined the Bournemouth Fire Brigade and then didn't see him again until he had retired.
Tommy was one of Britain's two gold medallists at that Games (Tommy Hampson was the other at 800metres) and he returned to a hero's welcome.

On the track Tom Hampson (Archilles Club) scored a great win in the 800m to crack the 1m 50sec. barrier by recording 1m 49.7sec. (rounded up to 1.49.8secs as times over this distance were only given in fifths of a second).
Scrimshaw distinguished himself by running second in his heat and fourth in the final, with T.
